contexts.text: A noise was heard as if of many waters, and a conflict among them... which originated from the confusion of opinions concerning certain Truths... Described, Explained.
The noise of his wheels () = sensuous things and their fallacies which urge on.
I heard a noise from them as of wood split up by the lire in a furnace.
I once heard beneath me as it were the noise of the sea. Explained.
At these words, a noise was made; but it was stilled by light descending from Heaven.
Whenever he moved, a noise was heard beneath, like the noise of punishings. Explained.
I will make the noise of thy songs to cease () = vastation as to the Knowledges of good.
The noise of songs () = the joys of confessions.
The noise of the peoples () = contradictions by falsities.
The voice of a noise, and a great tumult out of the land of the north () = falsities combating against truths, and evils against goods.
